core_claim.P: AtomWallet is an ERC-4337 smart contract wallet whose owner may be a smart contract (multisig, DAO, AtomWarden) rather than an EOA
core_claim.I: ERC-4337 UserOperation signature validation in _validateSignature must support smart-contract owners (e.g., via ERC-1271) so that valid owner signatures are accepted
core_claim.V: _validateSignature exclusively uses ECDSA.tryRecover and compares to owner(), so smart-contract owners cannot produce valid signatures and recovered != owner() always holds

direct_impacts.description: Once ownership is transferred to a multisig, the AtomWallet loses all AA capabilities and the DAO is permanently unable to route transactions through the EntryPoint, preventing use of Paymasters for gas sponsorship, batch operations, or automated claim executions
direct_impacts.evidence_quote: Once ownership is transferred to a multisig, the `AtomWallet` loses all AA capabilities. The DAO will be permanently unable to route transactions through the `EntryPoint`, meaning they cannot utilize Paymasters for gas sponsorship, batch operations, or automated claim executions.

direct_impacts.description: Newly minted AtomWallets are by default owned by the AtomWarden smart contract, so in their initial unclaimed state they inherently cannot interact with the ERC-4337 pipeline
direct_impacts.evidence_quote: Newly minted `AtomWallets` are by default owned by the `AtomWarden` (which is a smart contract). This implies that in its initial unclaimed state, the wallet inherently cannot interact with the ERC-4337 pipeline.
